A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLR framework and 20-level SLR-BENCH. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material that was moved or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original SLR-BENCH evaluations, inference costs and Llama fine-tuning results in Table 2 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 reports original SLR-BENCH evaluations and curriculum-training results, including downstream benchmark outcomes in Tables 3 and 4.

M1.justification: The synthesis algorithm, symbolic evaluation and cross-entropy objective remain substantively unchanged. The demonstrated training procedure changes from shuffled fine-tuning in v1 Section 5.2 to sequential, unshuffled curriculum training with LoRA in v3 Appendix G.1. Expanded descriptions of rule generation and syntax checking do not establish additional method changes.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates reasoning performance within the synthetic train domain. v3 Table 3 adds evaluations on MMLU and three subject subsets, LogiQA/LogiQA2, three GPQA variants, ARC-Easy, ARC and HellaSwag, substantially broadening task coverage. The original SLR-BENCH curriculum remains.

E2.justification: Relative to v1 Table 2, v3 Table 4 adds GPT-4-turbo and Llama-3.2-1B, while removing Internlm2-20B, Qwen2-57B, CodeLlama-34B and Mixtral-8x7B from the reported benchmark comparison. This substantially revises the conventional-model comparison set. DeepSeek-R1 and R1-Llama-70B denote the same distilled model according to both tables' footnotes.

E3.justification: v1 reports fine-tuning on 16,000 tasks sampled across all levels, including shuffled LoRA training. v3 Appendix G.1 reports approximately 17k examples presented in curriculum order and restricts training to basic/easy/medium splits with a 6k-token limit. Appendix G.2 introduces downstream evaluation using official splits and benchmark-default zero/few-shot settings. v3 omits v1's explicit 600-task evaluation subset, so a change to the leaderboard's test sample cannot be established.

E4.justification: v1 Table 2 compares full-parameter and LoRA fine-tuning of the same Llama model; v3 retains only the LoRA curriculum result, removing that adaptation comparison. Difficulty-tier and test-time-compute analyses remain. The new downstream scores do not include a controlled comparison of ordered versus shuffled training.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's additional results retain the point-estimate reporting practice of v1.

E6.justification: Several leaderboard values change: GPT-4.5-preview LRL changes from 7.2 to 7.6, GPT-4o from 6.7 to 6.4, and the distilled DeepSeek model from 8.1 to 8.8; OpenAI reasoning-model rows remain unchanged. The earlier FFT/LoRA results of 9.4/8.4 LRL are replaced by a curriculum-LoRA result of 8.8, and v3 adds downstream results, including MMLU 63.3 versus 66.1 for base versus tuned models. Changed training and incompletely matched evaluation settings prevent treating these as same-setting improvements across versions.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix F adds formal definitions of first-order terms, literals, clauses, interpretations and model-theoretic entailment beyond v1's shorter task formalization. The scoring equations remain substantively equivalent, and neither version provides theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: v1's training contribution concerns improved performance on SLR-BENCH. v3's abstract, introduction and conclusion extend this to curriculum learning that improves reasoning across established downstream benchmarks, substantially broadening the claimed contribution. The automated synthesis, controllable difficulty and symbolic evaluation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new benchmark results as evidence of transferable reasoning from curriculum training. It removes v1's speculation that limited hard-tier improvement reflects architectural capacity and may require architectural changes or search. The main semantic-error and compute interpretations, along with Section 7's train-domain, single-rule and synthetic-data limitations, remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds the LLM-guided generation prompt with extensive Prolog examples and substantially expands training/evaluation documentation: two epochs, eight GPUs, four-hour training, software frameworks, optimizer, learning rate, scheduler, batch size and memory settings. It also adds a separate dataset link and release/licensing statements. These are major documentation additions, although the leaderboard sample size becomes less explicit and Appendix H mixes present-release statements with availability after publication.

R1.justification: v3 adds foundational ILP references by Muggleton and de Raedt, Cropper and Dumančić, and Lloyd, plus references supporting the new evaluation and implementation material. Table 1 removes the bAbI and Multi-LogiEval rows while retaining discussion or citations elsewhere. The central positioning around flexible synthesis, controlled curricula and symbolic evaluation is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten or condensed. Section 5 is reorganized to foreground curriculum transfer, and the appendices are substantially expanded and reorganized. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds the verifiable-rewards diagram in Figure 2 and a separate training/transfer results table. The curriculum table moves from v1's appendix to the main text and is transposed into a horizontal layout; the leaderboard is restructured to separate tuning results. Existing pipeline, prompt, compute and synthesis-example figures are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The downstream evaluations in v3 Table 3 address v1's lack of evidence beyond the synthetic train domain, while Appendices E and G substantially improve the documentation available for reproduction. The overall gain is limited by the removed FFT comparison, lack of a matched shuffled-training control or uncertainty estimates for the expanded claims, and loss of the explicit leaderboard sample-size disclosure. These changes make the paper more informative without establishing a comparably strong increase in evidential rigor.
